issues.message: 已取得的英语词条还列出经济领域的“参与者、行为主体”义，原稿遗漏。此义不必列为初中核心义，可补入较少见义，且仅适用于 actor。
actors 的英式复数读音是 /ˈæk.təz/，常见美式读音是 /ˈæk.tɚz/；原稿把可选 r 放在 z 后，音序错误。
英式词尾 r“不明显”不够准确，应说明常见英式发音不读该 r，以及后接元音时的连读情况。
材料支持拉丁语来源形式 actor 和英语中14世纪见用，但没有提供拉丁语释义，也不能证明“演员”义在14世纪已经出现。应删除这两项未经支持的阶段说明，并把 act + -or 明确限定为现代拼写助记。
leading actor 可用于任何性别，直接译成“男主角”范围过窄；此处译为“主演”更符合本课的用法说明。
Oxford 未提供实际正文，Cambridge 本次获取失败。推荐标签不等于已核验；本次引用宜关联到实际取得的英语词条。act、acting 的常识性说明可以保留，但不应挂靠未取得正文的词典。

independence.basis: Read the complete candidate, author records/source summaries, original issue list and affected patch paths. Independently opened the supporting dictionary and etymology pages, then compared current wording and example coverage.

readScope: Every core and optional meaning; all bilingual examples, patterns/collocations and scoped comparisons; overview/study plan, IPA/forms, confusions, historical meanings and direction, family spellings, mnemonic, source metadata and editorial status.

linguisticFindings.detail: Actor covers performers of any gender; actress specifically denotes a woman. The two core examples are natural. Formal participation is broader than economics, and the small-business example is a valid instance. The politeness/surprise example demonstrates pretending without claiming professional acting.

Performer is broader; audience is only a theatre-role contrast. Actor and actress forms and plurals are correctly distinguished. The former plural r-placement error is absent; UK non-rhotic use and linking are explained. Modern act/-or and actress/-ress spellings are teaching mnemonics, not false historical coinage.

The Latin doer/agent/theatrical meanings and English earlier administrator use are now explicitly separated. The 16th-century English stage sense is not backdated to the 14th-century borrowing. Actress is not assigned the same chronological path.
